title: Target Renegade
build: Supplied OneLoad64 EasyFlash edition; cartridge SHA-256 4a15d0ee31f58427723170975a31bd05a900e9a5914bd84f8fc28c742e4ed924

records.c: Title loop: wait for raster line 100 to pass, call $07BF, animate the prompt colours, and test Space through $2833. Read CIA1 port B bit 4 for joystick-port-1 fire; a low bit leaves through $26E3 and eventually jumps to $8000.
Wait until raster register $D012 equals 100, then wait for it to differ. Return after that line has passed; this tests the low eight raster bits.
Copy the byte at $277A to 28 colour-RAM cells $DB7A-$DB95, then increment that byte. Called by the title loop for the start prompt.
Fixed 27-character title row copied by $2659-$2699: "WRITTEN  BY DAVE COLLIER   ".
Fixed 27-character title row copied by $2659-$2699: "GRAPHICS BY JOHN PALMER    ".
Fixed 27-character title row copied by $2659-$2699: "            MARTIN MCDONALD".
Fixed 27-character title row copied by $2659-$2699: "MUSIC    BY GARY BIASILLO  ".
Fixed 27-character title row copied by $2659-$2699: "CBM PAUSE    SPACE       ON".
Fixed 27-character title row copied by $2659-$2699: "PRESS FIRE TO START        ".

Input A is a key number (row times eight plus column). Save Y, select the row with $2870 and mask the column with $2878. Set carry when that column reads low with the row selected and high with all rows released; otherwise clear carry. Restore Y, return its value in A, and leave $DC00=$7F and $DC01=$FF. X is untouched.
Eight active-low row-selection masks, indexed by the top five bits of the key number passed to $2833 after three right shifts. Valid key numbers select indices 0-7.
Eight single-bit column masks, indexed by the low three bits of the key number in $2833.

Select RAM beneath BASIC and KERNAL with I/O visible ($01=$35). Store five in the lives byte $020C and clear stage and score bytes $0206/$0202/$0201 before calling game setup. Set the first extra-life threshold bytes to $05,$00 at $020A/$020B, copy $0200 to $0205, and enter the main loop after $803A. This describes the supplied EasyFlash edition.

Save A/Y/X to $07/$05/$06 and clear decimal mode. Acknowledge VIC interrupt flags with $FF. Use $09 as the phase index; increment it and reset it when the next byte in $AB15 is zero. Push the indexed high and low bytes from $AB2F, then RTS into that stored address plus one. The handler finishes through $ABE6.

Byte table read by phase handlers at $ABBA and $ABF9 to schedule the next raster interrupt. The dispatcher reads the following byte to detect a zero terminator. Contents can change with the display state; the entry snapshot records one state.
Twenty-six little-endian words indexed by twice the phase number in $AAF0. They are return-stack values: RTS enters each value plus one. Zero words are placeholders, not proven callable entries.

Wait while $D012 is at most $CF, then write $5F/$18/$DF to $D011/$D016/$D018 and $C3 to $DD00. Set extra background colours to $0A/$09 and schedule raster line $D5 before jumping to the shared interrupt return.
Wait while $D012 is at most $D5, write $1F to $D011, and schedule line $EE. Clear all eight sprite Y registers, then jump to the shared interrupt return.
Restore A/Y/X from $07/$05/$06 and return from the interrupt with RTI.

Schedule the next raster line from $AB15,Y and select VIC bank $4000 using $DD00=$C2. Set vertical scroll from $21 AND 7 with $D011 bit 4 set, horizontal scroll from $18 AND 7 with multicolour bit 4 set, and $D018 from $0609 OR 2. Finish through $ABE6.

Install the hardware IRQ vector $FFFE/$FFFF as $AAF0 and the NMI vector $FFFA/$FFFB as $A973. Enable VIC raster IRQ, disable and read CIA1 timer-A interrupt, clear phase $09, schedule raster line $F9, and enable CIA2 timer-A interrupt. Returns without executing CLI; the caller does so at $801D.

Input A supplies two nibbles and Y a character offset. Write the high nibble plus $30 and low nibble plus $30 to $3727,Y and the following cell. Advance Y twice and return; caller $FC3A/$FC40 uses this to draw the score. Nibbles are not validated as decimal digits.
